x-note: The reference host's demo stack (BE-005, UX-091; 06 §13; 13 §11.2): PostgreSQL, an S3-compatible store, the document service, one export worker with its sandbox image, and the reference host, seeded with a tenant, users and documents. Demo only: not a production deployment; every port is bound to 127.0.0.1 and the credentials are the test values of stack/.env.example. JSON is valid YAML, so `podman compose -f apps/reference-host/compose.json --env-file apps/reference-host/stack/.env.example up --build` reads this file where Compose works; scripts/stack.ps1 starts the same definitions on a machine where it does not (a WSL Podman machine needs --cgroups=disabled, which Compose cannot pass), running the Node.js services as local processes with the same commands. Services use host networking: on the WSL machine published ports are invisible to Windows, and binding 127.0.0.1 keeps everything local.
name: docedit-demo

postgres.x-note: PostgreSQL, as infra/containers/compose.base.json defines it for the integration tests too (FND-010 criterion 2). Data in a named volume, so documents and their history survive a restart (BE-005 criterion 5).

s3.x-note: The S3-compatible store, as infra/containers/compose.base.json defines it for the integration tests too. Exported PDFs live here (06 §4.2).

mail.x-note: The development mail sink (UX-098 criterion 5; owner decision 131): Mailpit takes every message the host sends and shows it in a web page and an API on 127.0.0.1, and delivers nothing. The image is pinned by digest in infra/containers/compose.base.json. Messages are kept in memory only, so a restart empties it.

setup.x-note: One-shot: secrets (generated, demo-only), the bucket and its CORS rules, the database, the service role, the migrations and the tenant registration (scripts/setup.ts). The only part that mounts every secret volume: the operator's complete record (secrets-operator) and one volume per role (SEC-048 criterion 2; owner decision 107). The other parts mount their own role's volume and nothing else; the export worker mounts none.

document-service.x-note: The document service as one process (BE-001): control plane, DEP WebSocket and rooms, on PostgreSQL and the S3 store, with the tenant seeded from the set-up's registration (BE-012).

seed.x-note: One-shot: the demo documents, created through the service with the host's externalId, their region grants, and the host's catalogue (scripts/seed.ts).

reference-host.x-note: The reference host (SvelteKit build behind scripts/serve.ts): demo sign-in, token endpoint, catalogue and the editor page.

export-worker.x-note: The export worker (services/export-worker, src/main.ts): claims export jobs from the queue in PostgreSQL, converts, and compiles each job in a fresh sandbox container of the image below, through the Podman socket of the machine. The worker process needs the database and the store; LuaLaTeX runs only in the sandbox, which has no network (09 §9.3; BE-005 criterion 4).

export-sandbox.x-note: The compile sandbox of 09 §9.3, built from services/export-worker/Containerfile (owned by the export work; referenced, not copied). The worker runs one container of it per job with these settings and its own limits (services/export-worker, src/sandbox.ts): a tar of the bundle in, a tar of the outputs out, no network. Here it only builds the image and checks it starts without network.
